questionText: What is another name for a folder in a computer?
correctAnswer: Directory
explanation: A folder, also called a directory, is a container used to store related files together. A drive is a hardware component that stores data, not another name for a folder.

questionText: What is a folder that is contained inside another folder called?
correctAnswer: A subfolder
explanation: A folder can contain another folder inside it, and a folder contained in another folder is called a subfolder. A shortcut is an icon that takes you to another place quickly.

questionText: Which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows?
correctAnswer: Windows key + E
explanation: You can use the Windows key + E keyboard shortcut to open File Explorer; it can also be opened from the taskbar icon or the Start menu.

questionText: Which key renames a selected file or folder?
correctAnswer: F2
explanation: After highlighting a file or folder, pressing the F2 key lets you rename it. The Delete key moves it to the Recycle Bin instead.

questionText: What file extension does Notepad give to a plain text file?
correctAnswer: .txt
explanation: Notepad saves any text file with the .txt extension, meaning no special formatting or fonts. .docx is used by word processors such as Microsoft Word.

questionText: Which application is the default image editing program in the Windows operating system?
correctAnswer: Microsoft Paint
explanation: Microsoft Paint is the default image editing application in Windows and can be used to simply edit an image file. Notepad is a text editor.

questionText: Which drive letter usually designates the hard disk drive?
correctAnswer: C:
explanation: A hard disk drive (hard disk or fixed disk) is usually designated as the C: drive, while a CD/DVD drive is usually D: or G:.

questionText: Where do deleted files go when they are deleted with only the Delete key?
correctAnswer: The Recycle Bin
explanation: Files deleted with the Delete key go to the Recycle Bin, where they can be restored unless permanently deleted. Quick Access only lists frequently used folders.

questionText: Which shortcut key cuts selected files so that they can be moved?
correctAnswer: Ctrl+X
explanation: Ctrl+X cuts the selected files to a temporary clipboard and Ctrl+V pastes them at the destination, which moves them. Ctrl+C copies instead of cutting.

questionText: Which section of the Navigation pane shows all the drives mounted on the computer?
correctAnswer: This PC
explanation: The This PC section of the Navigation pane contains all drives mounted on the computer. Network lets you see networked PCs.

questionText: How does a file differ from a folder?
options: A file holds related data; a folder holds files
A file can hold other folders, while a folder holds only data
A file never has an extension, while a folder always has one
A file is a hardware part, while a folder is a software program
correctAnswer: A file holds related data; a folder holds files
explanation: A file is a collection of interrelated data, whereas a folder is a container used to store files and subfolders. Files have extensions to identify their types, but folders do not.

questionText: Why do folders allow two files to have the same name?
options: Each file can sit in a different folder
Windows adds a hidden code to every name
Files with the same name merge into one
Folders store files without any names
correctAnswer: Each file can sit in a different folder
explanation: Folders allow more than one file with the same name, such as My-letter.doc in My Documents and another in Letter collection. If all files were in one place, every file would need a unique name.

questionText: StudentMarkList.pdf is copied into the same folder. What could the copy be named?
correctAnswer: StudentMarkList - Copy.pdf
explanation: A file name must be unique, so a number such as StudentMarkList (1).pdf or "- Copy" is appended to the copied file's name in the same folder. The extension stays .pdf.

questionText: What is the difference between Save and Save As?
options: Save updates the file; Save As saves to a new name or place
Save creates a new file, while Save As updates an existing one
Save stores only text, while Save As stores pictures too
Save works in Notepad, while Save As works only in Word
correctAnswer: Save updates the file; Save As saves to a new name or place
explanation: Save updates a previously saved file with new content, whereas Save As saves a new file or an existing file to a new location with the same or a different name.

questionText: Which part of File Explorer lets you preview an item, such as a photo, without opening it?
options: The Status bar at the bottom
correctAnswer: The Preview/Details pane
explanation: The Preview/Details pane lets you quickly preview an item such as a photo without opening it; it is not open by default. The Status bar shows the number and size of items.

questionText: Which part of File Explorer shows the total number of items in a folder, the number selected and the total file size?
correctAnswer: The Status bar
explanation: The Status bar displays information about a selected folder and its contents, such as the total number of items, the number selected and the total file size.

questionText: How can a folder be pinned to the Quick Access area?
options: Right-click it and select Pin to Quick access
Press F2 on the folder and type Quick access
Drag the folder into the Recycle Bin
Open the folder and press Ctrl+V
correctAnswer: Right-click it and select Pin to Quick access
explanation: To add or pin a folder to the Quick Access area, right-click the folder name and select Pin to Quick access. F2 renames a selected item.

questionText: In the Windows 10 Navigation pane, what does a right-pointing triangle next to a folder name show?
correctAnswer: The folder has subfolders
explanation: A right-pointing triangle means the folder has subfolders; no triangle means it has none, and a down-pointing triangle means its subfolders are currently displayed.

questionText: What happens when Shift + Delete is used on a file?
options: It is deleted for good, skipping the Recycle Bin
The file is moved to the Recycle Bin and can be restored later
The file is copied to the clipboard ready to be pasted elsewhere
The file is hidden but stays in its folder
correctAnswer: It is deleted for good, skipping the Recycle Bin
explanation: Holding Shift while pressing Delete deletes the files permanently; they do not go to the Recycle Bin, so restoring them from there is not possible.

questionText: What happens to the files inside a folder when that folder is deleted?
options: All files and folders inside it are deleted too
The files are moved to the Desktop automatically
The files stay where they were without the folder
Only the empty subfolders inside it are deleted
correctAnswer: All files and folders inside it are deleted too
explanation: If you delete a folder or directory, all files and folders in that folder are deleted, which is why you should check that it is empty first.

questionText: How does Linux represent drives and folders, unlike Windows drive letters?
options: As a tree whose root is a forward slash (/)
As a list of numbered drives starting from 0
As letters starting from A: for every drive
As separate windows for each storage device
correctAnswer: As a tree whose root is a forward slash (/)
explanation: Windows refers to drives by letters like C:, but Linux uses a tree structure starting from the root represented by a forward slash (/), with folders such as /home for users' files.

questionText: What is the difference between a drive and a driver?
options: A drive stores data; a driver lets hardware talk to the OS
A drive is software that runs the printer, while a driver stores programs
A drive is removable, while a driver is always built into the computer
A drive and a driver are two names for the same storage device
correctAnswer: A drive stores data; a driver lets hardware talk to the OS
explanation: A drive typically refers to a hard drive or solid-state drive used to store the operating system, data and programs, while a driver is software code that lets hardware devices communicate with the operating system.

questionText: How does moving a file differ from copying it?
options: Moving leaves only one copy, while copying makes a second copy
Moving makes a second copy, while copying leaves only one
Moving renames the file, while copying deletes the original one
Moving and copying both delete the file from its first place
correctAnswer: Moving leaves only one copy, while copying makes a second copy
explanation: When copying files you get more than one copy on your computer, while moving keeps only one copy at the new location. Copy and paste is therefore not the same as moving.

questionText: When moving files by right-dragging them, what must you choose after releasing the mouse button?
correctAnswer: Move here
explanation: With right-button drag-and-drop, a menu appears when you release the button, and you select Move here to move the files. Copy here would leave the originals in place.

questionText: Several files are selected and renamed at once by pressing F2 and typing test. What names do they get?
options: test, test (1), test (2) and so on
test1, test2, test3 and so on
test-a, test-b, test-c and so on
All of them get the identical name test
correctAnswer: test, test (1), test (2) and so on
explanation: Selecting several files and pressing F2 to type test renames them to test, test (1), test (2), test (3), and so on, keeping every name unique.

questionText: While renaming by clicking a selected file name a second time, why does the file sometimes open instead?
options: The second click came too fast and acted as a double-click
The file is locked because it is stored on the C: drive
The F2 key was pressed instead of the mouse button
Renaming by clicking only works for folders and never for files
correctAnswer: The second click came too fast and acted as a double-click
explanation: In this method you highlight the file, wait a few seconds and click the name again; if you do not wait long enough and click too fast, the file opens instead of allowing you to rename it.

questionText: Why should a flash drive be disconnected with Eject before it is pulled out of the USB port?
options: To avoid damaging files on the drive
To rename the flash drive automatically
To copy its files to the C: drive
correctAnswer: To avoid damaging files on the drive
explanation: You must make sure the flash drive is disconnected properly with Disconnect or Eject to avoid damaging files on the drive, and only then remove it from the USB port.

questionText: Which search method lets you find a file on one specific drive?
options: Click the drive under This PC, then search there
Press the Windows key and type the drive letter followed by F2
Open the Recycle Bin and sort the files by their drive letter
Open Notepad and use the Save As window to look for the file
correctAnswer: Click the drive under This PC, then search there
explanation: To find a file on a specific drive, click the drive under Computer or This PC in the Navigation pane, then enter the file name in the Search field; you do not need the full name.

questionText: Why do you need the right permissions to rename some files and folders?
options: It needs rights to the item, sometimes admin rights
Renaming always deletes the item's content, so it is restricted
Only files on removable drives can ever be renamed
Renaming moves the item to another drive, which needs a password
correctAnswer: It needs rights to the item, sometimes admin rights
explanation: You must have rights or permissions to a file, folder or directory to rename it, and in some cases administrator privileges. Renaming does not remove a file's content.

questionText: Which browsers put downloaded files by default in the Download folder reached from Quick Access?
options: Internet Explorer, Microsoft Edge and Chrome
Notepad, WordPad and the Microsoft Paint program
File Explorer, This PC and OneDrive
correctAnswer: Internet Explorer, Microsoft Edge and Chrome
explanation: Browsers such as Internet Explorer, Microsoft Edge and Chrome put all files downloaded from the Internet in the Download folder by default, which can be opened from Quick Access.
